title: Failing over from one region to another, and failing back
captions: Active-passive. All writes go to Mumbai. Singapore keeps a copy that is about one second behind, and serves only reads.
The Mumbai region fails. The writes from its last second never reached Singapore. If you fail over now, those writes are missing.
First stop the old writer from taking writes. This is fencing. Then promote Singapore to be the writer. Skip the fence, and you risk split-brain.
Point DNS at Singapore. Clients that cached the old answer move later. Singapore must now carry all the load, plus a flood of retries.
When Mumbai comes back, do not trust its data as it is. Rebuild it as a copy of Singapore. Then look in its old data for writes that never got copied.
Failing back is a separate, planned move. Wait until Mumbai has fully caught up, then switch roles at a quiet hour, with no data lost.
